must_do: read the spec first and stop if it is missing — the router orders spec before domain
identify the Moment-Intervals first (read the spec's scenarios as events), and get that list approved before deriving anything else
map each archetype onto the kit: MI -> Repository method + ViewModel action (never a UseCase class, Rule 9), PPT -> data/model/*Response.kt, Role -> field/nested object, Description -> enum
mark every derived attribute (a count that is an aggregation, a rank that is a position in a sort) explicitly as derived rather than stored
write exactly one file, openspec/changes/<id>/domain.md, then re-run kmp_route.py so .kmp/route.json sees it
record `Domain model: none` with one sentence when the capability genuinely has no domain concepts
must_not: start from the spec's nouns / entity list instead of Moment-Intervals
model a Moment-Interval as a UseCase class (Rule 9 forbids the UseCase layer)
add a parallel Response DTO for something that is a Role on an existing party
invent a requirement to fill a table — a gap goes under Open questions with the default taken
edit feature/**, the spec, or the design; this skill writes only domain.md
omit domain.md silently when the model is trivial — silence is indistinguishable from skipping it

pass_criteria: domain.md exists in the change directory with Moment-Intervals first, every derived attribute marked, a filled archetype->KMP mapping table, and no UseCase layer; re-running kmp_route.py reports artifacts.domain present.

should: what should the data model be
